description: Stellar Experience reúne ingeniería de sistemas, UX/UI y diseño de marketing para convertir un reto espacial en una experiencia interactiva, clara y divertida para jóvenes astronautas.
summary: ASU STELLAR · Horizonte is a free 3D browser game in which children aged 7–12 plan and run a base on the Moon and on Mars. Players load the rocket with power, air, water, food and shielding within a real mass budget, predict what will fail, launch, and then advance day by day through the long lunar night, a Martian dust storm and the real May 2024 solar storm. When the base fails, the game shows the chain of causes and a NASA fact, and players can rewind to any day or redesign. Every number comes from a cited NASA source. A short pre- and post-test, a case rubric and a teacher panel measure learning, so teachers in places like Moquegua, Peru can use it in class even with older phones and no internet. It matters because astronauts learn space as trade-offs, and children can now practise that safely.
details:
What it does. A campaign of Episode 0 (coached tutorial) plus four missions from the Moon to Mars, and three extra challenges. Each mission is a loop: design the base under the rocket's mass limit, predict the outcome, watch the launch, the journey (4 days like Apollo 11, about 7 months like Perseverance) and the landing, advance day by day, and if something fails, read the chain of causes with a NASA fact card, then redesign or rewind with the Chronoscope. Leftover supplies become the reserve for the next mission. Players explore the lunar surface (ice crater, lava-tube pit, fresh crater, rover, antenna), see the real site of each mission on a 3D globe of the Moon and Mars, and earn stellar credits and 12 badges for good predictions, not rewinding and learning from a mistake, which they spend on suits, patches and accessories for their crew.

How it works. A deterministic simulation (40 automated tests) computes energy, oxygen, water, food, radiation and science every day from 22 NASA figures stored with their source, date and link. The 3D world uses Three.js and lowers its own quality on slow devices, down to a light 2D view that keeps the mission running. It is an installable web app that works offline. A small Node.js server with SQLite saves each student's progress under a class code and powers the teacher panel: teachers create their own class with their own key, students join with a QR code, and the teacher can pause the class and see predictions, journals, badges and CSV exports. A demo classroom lets anyone try it.

Why it matters in Peru. In PISA 2022 Peru scored 408 points in science against an OECD average of 485, and 52.6% of 15-year-olds were below the baseline level 2. Yet in PISA 2015 Peru was among the countries with the most students expecting a science career: the interest is there, the competence is not. Even in Moquegua, one of the top regions in national assessments, three out of four 8th-grade students were below the expected level in science in 2022. Only 3 in 10 STEM graduates in Peru are women, and more than a third of households have no internet. HORIZONTE follows the three science competencies of Peru's National Curriculum with a STEAM approach and contributes to SDG 4 (quality education), SDG 5 (gender equality) and SDG 10 (reduced inequalities).

Benefits and intended impact. It turns space science into systems thinking: children see that batteries, water and shielding compete for the same mass, and that failure is information. It speaks Peruvian Spanish and US English with offline narration, passed an automated WCAG 2 A/AA audit, and runs on low-end phones without internet, which is the reality of many classrooms in our region. Its heroine is a Peruvian astronaut. Next step: a pilot with real classes in Moquegua.

Tools. HTML, CSS and JavaScript modules (no framework), Three.js r170, Web Audio (generated music), Node.js 22 with SQLite, Docker and Traefik on a VPS, Playwright and axe-core for testing, Piper TTS and Kokoro-82M for the voices, Whisper to verify them.
